questions.q: The bunch of keys __________ (is / are) on the hook.
The pupils in the front row __________ (was / were) whispering.
Neither of the answers __________ (is / are) acceptable.
Each of the girls __________ (have / has) a locker.
Physics __________ (is / are) harder than I expected.
The news about the floods __________ (was / were) alarming.
A number of parents __________ (was / were) waiting outside.
The number of complaints __________ (has / have) fallen.
My spectacles __________ (is / are) on the table.
A pair of gloves __________ (is / are) in the drawer.
There __________ (is / are) several reasons for the delay.
Fifty dollars __________ (is / are) too much for a cap.
questions.tip: A sum of money is one amount.

questions.q: Rice and curry __________ (is / are) my favourite lunch.
The choir __________ (is / are) rehearsing in the hall.
Everybody in the class __________ (want / wants) to go.
The captain, along with his players, __________ (was / were) interviewed.
questions.tip: 'Along with' does not change the subject.

questions.q: Half of the cake __________ (was / were) left.
Half of the biscuits __________ (was / were) left.
He is one of the boys who __________ (swim / swims) daily.
She is the only one of the girls who __________ (play / plays) chess.
Neither the coach nor the players __________ (was / were) happy.
Neither the players nor the coach __________ (was / were) happy.
Mathematics and Science __________ (is / are) compulsory.
The furniture in the flat __________ (was / were) very old.
Ten kilometres __________ (is / are) a long way to cycle.
Every one of the exhibits __________ (was / were) labelled.
The committee __________ (is / are) divided over the proposal.
questions.tip: Here the members act as individuals.

questions.q: A great deal of effort __________ (has / have) gone into this.
Not one of the windows __________ (was / were) open.
Three-quarters of the field __________ (has / have) been flooded.
My trousers __________ (need / needs) mending.
The box of old photographs __________ (was / were) in the attic.
Measles __________ (is / are) a serious illness.
questions.tip: An illness ending in -es can still be singular.

questions.q: There __________ (was / were) hardly any milk left.
Both of my cousins __________ (live / lives) in Penang.
Either of the two routes __________ (is / are) acceptable.
The scissors __________ (is / are) blunt.
"The Three Musketeers" __________ (is / are) a wonderful story.
Two hours __________ (is / are) enough time for the test.
My brother's shoes __________ (is / are) under the bed.
None of the pupils __________ (was / were) absent today.
questions.tip: With a plural noun, 'were' is now standard.

questions.q: The herd of buffalo __________ (was / were) moving slowly.
Politics __________ (interest / interests) my father a great deal.
A lot of rubbish __________ (was / were) found in the drain.
A lot of bottles __________ (was / were) found in the drain.
Somebody __________ (have / has) taken my umbrella.
The jury __________ (is / are) still arguing among themselves.
Each boy and girl __________ (was / were) given a prize.
My aunt, as well as my uncle, __________ (is / are) coming.
questions.tip: 'As well as' does not add to the subject.

questions.q: Twenty per cent of the class __________ (was / were) late.
questions.tip: 'Class' here means the pupils in it.

questions.q: My mother __________ (leave) for work at seven every day.
Listen! The neighbours __________ (argue) again.
We __________ (fly) to Penang last June.
By the time we arrived, the film __________ (start).
questions.tip: The earlier of two past actions.

questions.q: She __________ (work) here since 2019.
I __________ (already / finish) my revision.
He __________ (not see) her since the holidays.
Ice __________ (melt) at zero degrees Celsius.
I will phone you as soon as I __________ (arrive).
Look at that sky! It __________ (pour) any minute.
The train __________ (depart) at 6.15 tomorrow morning.
While Father __________ (mow) the lawn, I washed the car.
They __________ (know) each other for twelve years.
Before he left, he __________ (switch) off all the lights.
I __________ (never / taste) anything so sour.
She __________ (do) her homework at the moment.
My grandfather __________ (teach) for thirty years before he retired.
If it __________ (snow), the flight will be cancelled.
questions.tip: First conditional — no 'will' in the if-clause.

questions.q: He __________ (lie) on the sofa when I came in.
She __________ (lay) the table before the guests arrived.
The sun __________ (rise) at about seven in December.
By next April, I __________ (complete) my primary education.
I __________ (write) three letters so far this week.
He __________ (break) his wrist last Tuesday.
We __________ (wait) for two hours before the doctor called us.
My sister __________ (stay) with our aunt this month.
Water __________ (freeze) if you leave it outside tonight.
Nobody __________ (tell) me about the change.
They __________ (build) the bridge in 1998.
I __________ (not understand) the question.
The pupils __________ (sing) when the bell rang.
He __________ (forget) his password again.
She __________ (swim) every morning before school.
We __________ (visit) the museum tomorrow afternoon.
He __________ (stop) the car so suddenly that I jolted forward.
I __________ (see) that film twice already.
The children __________ (play) outside since breakfast.
My father __________ (drive) us to school yesterday.
By the end of last term, she __________ (read) eleven books.
I __________ (wash) the dishes when the phone __________ (ring).
questions.tip: Long action interrupted by a short one.

questions.q: He __________ (carry) the boxes upstairs an hour ago.
We __________ (live) in this flat for six years now.
She __________ (not come) to the rehearsal last night.
The bell __________ (go) just as I reached the gate.
Wait here until I __________ (return).
My cousin __________ (grow) two centimetres since June.
He __________ (hurt) his ankle during the warm-up.
The choir __________ (practise) every Wednesday.
I __________ (just / hear) the good news.
By the time you read this, I __________ (leave) for Kuala Lumpur.
The concert begins __________ 7.30 p.m.
We are going away __________ the June holidays.
My birthday falls __________ 3 September.
Please finish this __________ Friday at the latest.
She has been unwell __________ Monday.
She has been unwell __________ four days.
Wait __________ six o'clock and then start without me.
The keys are __________ the kitchen drawer.
There is a poster __________ the classroom wall.
I will meet you __________ the bus stop.
He sat __________ his two sisters.
She was lost somewhere __________ the crowd.
The cat leapt __________ the fence and vanished.
We walked __________ the tunnel to the other side.
The tunnel runs __________ the whole length of the hill.
The library is __________ the post office.
__________ Mathematics, I also enjoy Art.
She sat down __________ the river and watched the boats.
Success depends __________ hard work.
He is very good __________ Science.
I apologised __________ the librarian __________ being noisy.
questions.tip: Apologise TO a person FOR a thing.

questions.q: My sister is afraid __________ heights.
Please look __________ my plants while I am away.
The police are looking __________ the theft.
His views are quite different __________ mine.
They congratulated her __________ winning the prize.
The kit consists __________ a bat, a ball and two stumps.
He has suffered __________ asthma since childhood.
I do not believe __________ ghosts.
She finally succeeded __________ opening the jar.
Careless driving often results __________ accidents.
The delay resulted __________ a signalling fault.
He was accused __________ cheating.
Do not blame her __________ the mistake.
They complained __________ the noise from the flat above.
My father insisted __________ paying for everyone.
A locked gate prevents anyone __________ entering.
That song reminds me __________ my grandmother.
We are relying __________ you to bring the tickets.
I agree __________ you about the timing.
They finally agreed __________ a date for the outing.
She was angry __________ her brother for taking her charger.
He was angry __________ the decision.
We arrived __________ the airport two hours early.
They arrived __________ Japan on Tuesday.
We discussed __________ the problem for an hour. (write X if no preposition is needed)
He entered __________ the hall quietly. (write X if no preposition is needed)
She reached __________ home just before the storm. (write X if no preposition is needed)
I am grateful __________ you __________ all your help.
questions.tip: Grateful TO a person FOR a thing.

questions.q: __________ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
__________ the traffic was heavy, we arrived on time.
He was exhausted; __________, he finished the race.
questions.tip: Finishing while exhausted is a contrast, which needs a contrast linker; 'so' and 'therefore' both show result.

questions.q: She revised for weeks; __________, she scored full marks.
questions.tip: Full marks followed from weeks of revising, so a result linker is needed, not a contrast one.

questions.q: __________ you apologise, she will not speak to you.
Hurry up, __________ we will miss the ferry.
questions.tip: This warns of the bad alternative if they do not hurry; 'and' would simply join two equal actions.

questions.q: The shop was closed, __________ we went home.
questions.tip: The closed shop caused them to go home, so a result conjunction fits; 'because' would reverse cause and effect.

questions.q: He is not only a fine pianist __________ also a gifted teacher.
questions.tip: 'Not only' is always paired with 'but also' — a fixed pattern worth learning by heart.

questions.q: Neither Ravi __________ Siti attended the rehearsal.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor', just as 'either' pairs with 'or'.

questions.q: __________ she was tired, she kept going.
questions.tip: A full clause follows, so a contrast conjunction is needed; 'Despite' and 'In spite of' need noun phrases.

questions.q: We cancelled the picnic __________ the forecast.
We cancelled the picnic __________ it was going to rain.
The road was closed; __________, we took a detour.
questions.tip: The detour resulted from the closed road, so a result linker fits; 'however' would signal contrast instead.

questions.q: She speaks Malay well; __________, her written Malay is weak.
questions.tip: Speaking well but writing weakly is a contrast, so a contrast linker fits, not the result words.

questions.q: __________ he had practised for months, he forgot his lines.
questions.tip: A full clause follows, so the contrast conjunction fits; 'Despite' and 'In spite of' must be followed by nouns.

questions.q: Take an umbrella __________ it rains.
questions.tip: The umbrella is a precaution against possible rain, which this phrase shows; 'unless' means 'if not'.

questions.q: He left early __________ he could catch the first bus.
questions.tip: Catching the first bus is his purpose, and purpose before a clause needs 'so that'; 'in order' needs 'to'.

questions.q: __________ the bell rang, the pupils rushed out.
questions.tip: A time link before a clause is needed; 'Scarcely', 'No sooner' and 'Hardly' all require inverted word order.

questions.q: No sooner had the bell rung __________ the pupils rushed out.
Hardly had she sat down __________ the phone rang.
The soup was __________ salty that nobody could finish it.
questions.tip: 'So' goes straight before an adjective, as in 'so salty that'; 'such' needs a noun phrase.

questions.q: It was __________ a salty soup that nobody could finish it.
questions.tip: Before 'a' plus adjective plus noun, 'such' is used, and 'so' cannot go there.

questions.q: __________ I finish my homework, may I go out?
questions.tip: Going out depends on a condition, and this phrase means 'only if'; 'unless' would reverse the meaning.

questions.q: He works hard; __________, he is always the last to leave.
questions.tip: 'Indeed' adds emphasis, confirming just how hard he works; 'however' would wrongly signal contrast.

questions.q: __________ of the delay, the guests remained cheerful.
We must leave now; __________, we shall be late.
questions.tip: 'Otherwise' means 'if we do not', warning what will happen; 'therefore' would show a result instead.

questions.q: She has two jobs; __________, she still finds time to volunteer.
questions.tip: Volunteering despite two jobs is a contrast, so a contrast linker is needed, not the three result words.

questions.q: __________ we had eaten, we went for a walk.
questions.tip: The walk came after the meal, so a time conjunction showing the earlier action is needed.

questions.q: He waited __________ everyone had left.
questions.tip: 'Until' marks the point at which the waiting stopped; the others show contrast or condition.

questions.q: The project failed __________ poor planning.
questions.tip: A noun phrase follows, so 'owing to' fits; 'because' would need a full clause after it.

questions.q: __________ she is only nine, she reads adult novels.
questions.tip: A full clause follows, so 'Although' fits; 'Due to', 'Despite' and 'In spite of' all need noun phrases.

questions.q: We had neither a map __________ a compass.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor', never with 'or' or 'and'.

questions.q: He was late; __________, the meeting had already started.
questions.tip: This phrase tells us when the meeting had started — before he arrived; the others add or contrast.

questions.q: __________ walking to school, he also cycles at weekends.
questions.tip: 'Besides' means 'in addition to' before an '-ing' word; 'Beside' means next to something.

questions.q: __________ the two of them, the job was finished in an hour.
questions.tip: 'Between' is used for two people, while 'among' is for three or more.

questions.q: She practises daily; __________, her playing has improved greatly.
questions.tip: Her improvement came from practising daily, so a result linker is needed, not a contrast one.

questions.q: __________ he tried, he could not open the jar.
questions.tip: 'However hard' means 'no matter how hard', which is the pattern being tested here.

questions.q: The film was long; __________, it held our attention throughout.
questions.tip: 'Even so' means 'despite that', showing contrast with the film's length; the other three all signal result.

questions.q: __________ finishing the race, she had to withdraw.
questions.tip: This shows one thing replacing another before an '-ing' word; 'Despite finishing' would mean she did finish.

questions.q: He apologised, __________ the damage was already done.
questions.tip: 'But' shows the contrast between apologising and the damage remaining; 'so' would wrongly signal result.

questions.q: Nadia and __________ (me / I) are in the same team.
The prize was given to Devan and __________ (me / I).
Between you and __________ (me / I), the plan will not work.
__________ (Who / Whom) did you give the letter to?
The girl __________ won the medal is my neighbour.
The boy __________ bag was stolen reported it.
This jacket is __________ (her / hers).
__________ (Its / It's) been raining all morning.
The bird built __________ (its / it's) nest in the drainpipe.
They built the treehouse __________ (theirselves / themselves).
Everyone should bring __________ own calculator.
Neither of the boys brought __________ swimming trunks.
__________ (We / Us) pupils were given extra time.
The teacher praised __________ (we / us) for our effort.
She is taller than __________ (me / I am).
questions.tip: 'Than I am' is the safer written form.

questions.q: That is __________ (a / an) honour I did not expect.
He is __________ (a / an) university student.
We waited for __________ (a / an) hour.
She plays __________ piano beautifully.
We had __________ dinner at eight. (write X if no article is needed)
He goes to __________ bed at nine. (write X if no article is needed)
__________ Himalayas are the highest mountain range.
There were __________ (fewer / less) pupils at the talk than expected.
There was __________ (fewer / less) noise after the bell.
__________ (Much / Many) of the equipment was damaged.
He has __________ (few / a few) friends and is often lonely.
He has __________ (few / a few) friends who visit every week.
She has __________ (little / a little) patience with latecomers.
Add __________ (little / a little) salt to the soup.
__________ (Every / All) pupil must sign the form.
__________ (Every / All) pupils must sign the form.
__________ (Either / Both) of the two answers is acceptable.
__________ (Either / Both) of the two answers are acceptable.
She spent __________ (a large amount of / a large number of) money.
She met __________ (a large amount of / a large number of) people.
__________ (Somebody / Some body) has left the tap running.
I have __________ (any / some) questions about the project.
I do not have __________ (any / some) questions.
__________ (This / These) scissors belong to the art room.
__________ (That / Those) news was unexpected.
You __________ (must not / need not) swim here; there is a strong current.
You __________ (must not / need not) bring a calculator; one will be provided.
She can __________ (plays / play) three instruments.
We __________ (will can / will be able to) finish by Friday.
questions.tip: Two modals cannot be used together.

questions.q: __________ (May / Must) I leave the table, please?
You __________ (should / must) have told me sooner; now it is too late.
questions.tip: 'Should have' = ought to have but didn't.

questions.q: As a boy my father __________ (can / could) recite the whole poem.
You __________ (should / may) see a dentist about that tooth.
He __________ (must / can) be at home — his shoes are outside.
Pupils __________ (have to / might) wear the school uniform.
It __________ (might / must) rain later, so take an umbrella.
__________ (Shall / Will) we start now?
You __________ (ought to / must) apologise to her.
I __________ (would / will) rather walk than wait for the bus.
He __________ (could / can) have been injured if he had fallen.
questions.tip: Past possibility that did not happen.

questions.q: You __________ (need not / must not) have waited; I had a key.
__________ (Could / Must) you pass me the salt, please?
She __________ (cannot / need not) be serious!
Visitors __________ (may not / need not) use the staff lift.
I __________ (must / should) admit that I was wrong.
She is your cousin, __________?
They haven't replied, __________?
You locked the door, __________?
Let's begin, __________?
I am next in the queue, __________?
Nobody telephoned, __________?
Shut the gate, __________?
There isn't any sugar left, __________?
There were forty entries, __________?
He can swim, __________?
She has finished, __________?
You will remember, __________?
Everyone enjoyed the trip, __________?
Nothing was damaged, __________?
He hardly ever complains, __________?
Don't be late, __________?
This is your bag, __________?
We must leave now, __________?
She used to live here, __________?
You would help me, __________?
Rewrite in the passive: The gardener waters the plants every morning.
questions.m: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning
questions.tip: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: Someone has taken my umbrella.
Rewrite in the passive: The council is repairing the pavement.
questions.m: The pavement is being repaired by the council

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: They will announce the winners on Friday.
questions.m: The winners will be announced on Friday

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: The dog had chewed the slipper.
questions.m: The slipper had been chewed by the dog

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: Mother is baking a cake.
questions.m: A cake is being baked by Mother

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: You must sign the form.
questions.tip: Modal passive: must be + past participle.

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: She gave me a book.
questions.m: I was given a book by her
questions.tip: Also accept: A book was given to me by her.

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: A bee stung him.
questions.m: He was stung by a bee

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: People grow rice in many parts of Asia.
questions.m: Rice is grown in many parts of Asia

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: The teacher has marked all the papers.
questions.m: All the papers have been marked by the teacher

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: Nobody has cleaned the windows.
questions.m: The windows have not been cleaned
questions.tip: A negative subject becomes a negative verb.

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: They are building a new library.
questions.m: A new library is being built

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: The storm damaged several roofs.
questions.m: Several roofs were damaged by the storm

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: We can solve this problem easily.
questions.m: This problem can be solved easily

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: Someone left the tap running all night.
questions.m: The tap was left running all night

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: The pupils have planted forty saplings.
questions.m: Forty saplings have been planted by the pupils

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: My uncle repairs watches.
questions.m: Watches are repaired by my uncle

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: They should have warned us.
Rewrite in the passive: The committee is considering three proposals.
questions.m: Three proposals are being considered by the committee

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: The letter was written by my grandfather.
Rewrite in the active: The trees were planted by the volunteers.
Rewrite in the active: The window has been broken by the boys.
questions.m: The boys have broken the window

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: The results will be released by the school.
questions.m: The school will release the results

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: The cake was being decorated by my sister.
questions.m: My sister was decorating the cake

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: The road is swept by the cleaners every morning.
questions.m: The cleaners sweep the road every morning

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: I was told the news by Nadia.
Rewrite in the active: The form must be completed by all applicants.
questions.m: All applicants must complete the form

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: The bicycle had been stolen by two men.
questions.m: Two men had stolen the bicycle

questions.q: Rewrite in the active: English is spoken here.
questions.tip: When the doer is unknown, use 'people' or 'they'.

questions.q: "I am tired," said Ravi.
"We are leaving now," they said.
questions.m: They said (that) they were leaving then

questions.q: "I finished it yesterday," she said.
questions.m: She said (that) she had finished it the day before

questions.q: "I will call you tomorrow," he said.
questions.m: He said (that) he would call me the next day

questions.q: "I have lost my ticket," the man said.
questions.m: The man said (that) he had lost his ticket

questions.q: "I can swim," the boy said.
questions.m: The boy said (that) he could swim

questions.q: "I may be late," she said.
questions.m: She said (that) she might be late

questions.q: "You must wear a helmet," the coach said.
questions.m: The coach said (that) we had to wear a helmet

questions.q: "Where do you live?" she asked.
"When did you arrive?" he asked.
questions.m: He asked when I had arrived

questions.q: "Are you coming?" she asked.
questions.m: She asked whether I was coming

questions.q: "Have you eaten?" Mother asked.
questions.m: Mother asked whether I had eaten

questions.q: "Why are you laughing?" the teacher asked.
questions.m: The teacher asked why I was laughing

questions.q: "Sit down," the teacher said.
questions.m: The teacher told us to sit down

questions.q: "Don't touch that," he warned.
questions.m: He warned me not to touch that

questions.q: "Please help me," she said.
questions.m: She asked me to help her

questions.q: "Let's go swimming," he said.
questions.tip: Also accept: suggested that we should go swimming.

questions.q: "What a beautiful view!" she said.
questions.m: She exclaimed that it was a beautiful view

questions.q: "The earth orbits the sun," the teacher said.
questions.m: The teacher said (that) the earth orbits the sun
questions.tip: No tense shift for a general truth.

questions.q: "I saw her last week," he said.
questions.m: He said (that) he had seen her the week before

questions.q: "I am going to Japan next month," she said.
questions.m: She said (that) she was going to Japan the following month

questions.q: "Do not be late again," the principal said.
questions.m: The principal told us not to be late again

questions.q: "How much does it cost?" the tourist asked.
questions.m: The tourist asked how much it cost

questions.q: "I have never been abroad," my aunt said.
questions.m: My aunt said (that) she had never been abroad

questions.q: "Bring your own water bottle," the teacher reminded us.
questions.m: The teacher reminded us to bring our own water bottles

questions.q: "Who broke the window?" the caretaker demanded.
questions.m: The caretaker demanded to know who had broken the window

questions.q: "I did not take it," the boy insisted.
questions.m: The boy insisted that he had not taken it

questions.q: "Congratulations on your result," she said.
questions.m: She congratulated me on my result

questions.q: "I am sorry I forgot," he said.
"This is my seat," the woman said.
questions.m: The woman said (that) that was her seat

questions.q: Combine: The woman is a doctor. She lives next door.
questions.m: The woman who lives next door is a doctor

questions.q: Combine: I read the book. You lent it to me.
questions.m: I read the book which you lent me

questions.q: Combine: That is the boy. His father is a pilot.
questions.m: That is the boy whose father is a pilot

questions.q: Combine: This is the park. We played here as children.
questions.m: This is the park where we played as children

questions.q: Combine: I remember the day. We met on that day.
questions.m: I remember the day when we met

questions.q: Combine: My uncle is an architect. He built this house. (non-defining)
questions.m: My uncle, who built this house, is an architect

questions.q: Combine: The man was arrested. The police were hunting for him.
questions.m: The man whom the police were hunting for was arrested

questions.q: Combine: She has a brother. He teaches at my school.
questions.m: She has a brother who teaches at my school

questions.q: Combine: The film was disappointing. Everyone praised it.
questions.m: The film which everyone praised was disappointing

questions.q: Combine: This is the shop. Its owner won the award.
questions.m: This is the shop whose owner won the award

questions.q: Combine: The bus was full. It stopped outside our block.
questions.m: The bus which stopped outside our block was full

questions.q: Combine: I spoke to the girl. Her bicycle was stolen.
questions.m: I spoke to the girl whose bicycle was stolen

questions.q: Combine: The cake was delicious. My grandmother baked it.
questions.m: The cake which my grandmother baked was delicious

questions.q: Combine: Mr Rahim teaches Science. He coaches the football team.
questions.m: Mr Rahim, who coaches the football team, teaches Science

questions.q: Combine: This is the restaurant. We celebrated her birthday here.
questions.m: This is the restaurant where we celebrated her birthday

questions.q: Combine: The pupils were praised. They cleared the classroom.
questions.m: The pupils who cleared the classroom were praised

questions.q: Combine: I have lost the pen. My father gave it to me.
questions.m: I have lost the pen which my father gave me

questions.q: Combine: The house is for sale. We used to live in it.
questions.m: The house which we used to live in is for sale
questions.tip: Also accept: in which we used to live.

questions.q: Combine: She is the only pupil. She answered every question.
questions.m: She is the only pupil who answered every question

questions.q: Combine: I met a woman. Her son is in my class.
questions.m: I met a woman whose son is in my class

questions.q: Combine: The letter arrived today. I had been waiting for it.
questions.m: The letter which I had been waiting for arrived today

questions.q: Combine: That is the coach. He trained the national team.
questions.m: That is the coach who trained the national team

questions.q: Combine: The road is closed. It leads to the beach.
questions.m: The road which leads to the beach is closed

questions.q: Combine: My cousin lives in Perth. She is visiting next month. (non-defining)
questions.m: My cousin, who lives in Perth, is visiting next month

questions.q: Combine: We visited the museum. It had just reopened. (non-defining)
questions.m: We visited the museum, which had just reopened

questions.q: Combine: The girl was awarded a scholarship. Her essay won first prize.
questions.m: The girl whose essay won first prize was awarded a scholarship

questions.q: Combine: I still have the watch. My grandfather wore it.
questions.m: I still have the watch which my grandfather wore

questions.q: Combine: Those are the neighbours. We borrowed their ladder.
questions.m: Those are the neighbours whose ladder we borrowed

questions.q: Combine: The year was 2020. The library closed that year.
questions.m: The year when the library closed was 2020

questions.q: Combine: He is the man. I told you about him.
questions.m: He is the man whom I told you about
questions.tip: Also accept: about whom I told you.

questions.q: Passage 10 — Every Sunday morning, my mother and me go to the wet market.
questions.tip: The error was “me”. It is part of the subject.

questions.q: Passage 10 — We leave the flat at seven, before the crowd arrive.
questions.tip: The error was “arrive”. 'Crowd' is singular here.

questions.q: Passage 10 — The market is only a ten minutes walk from our block.
questions.tip: The error was “minutes”. A compound adjective takes the singular.

questions.q: Passage 10 — My mother always buy the vegetables first.
questions.tip: The error was “buy”. Third person singular.

questions.q: Passage 10 — She says that the freshest produce are sold by nine o'clock.
Passage 10 — Last week we bought two kilogram of prawns.
Passage 10 — The fishmonger, who has known us for years, gave us a discount.
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 10 — My mother was very please with the price.
questions.tip: The error was “please”. It describes how she felt.

questions.q: Passage 10 — On the way home, the bag tore and the prawns fell out.
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 10 — We had to pick them up quick before a cat appeared.
questions.tip: The error was “quick”. It describes how we picked them up.

questions.q: Passage 10 — Although we laughed about it, my mother was annoy.
questions.tip: The error was “annoy”. It describes how she felt.

questions.q: Passage 10 — Now we always bring a spare bag, just in case.
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 11 — Our school library have more than eight thousand books.
Passage 11 — It is open from Monday to Friday, exept during examinations.
Passage 11 — Each pupil are allowed to borrow four books at a time.
Passage 11 — Last term I borrow eleven novels altogether.
Passage 11 — Mrs Fong, the librarian, recommend a mystery series to me.
Passage 11 — I finished the first book in two day.
Passage 11 — The plot was so exciting that I could not put it down.
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 11 — Since than, I have read every book in the series.
questions.tip: The error was “than”. 'Then' refers to time.

questions.q: Passage 11 — My friends often asks me for recommendations.
Passage 11 — I have decided to join the library committee nex year.
Passage 12 — Our class was ask to plan a small concert for Teachers' Day.
questions.tip: The error was “ask”. Passive needs the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 12 — We formed four group of eight pupils each.
Passage 12 — My group decided to perform a dance, which were my idea.
questions.tip: The error was “were”. 'Which' refers to the idea.

questions.q: Passage 12 — We practise every lunchtime for three weeks.
Passage 12 — Nadia, who dances beautiful, led the routine.
questions.tip: The error was “beautiful”. It describes how she dances.

questions.q: Passage 12 — On the day itself, I was extremely nervous but exciting.
questions.tip: The error was “exciting”. It describes how I felt.

questions.q: Passage 12 — The audience clapped loud when we finished.
questions.tip: The error was “loud”. It describes how they clapped.

questions.q: Passage 12 — Our form teacher said she was very proud in us.

passages.text:
The Broken Window

Nobody in our block knows (1)______ broke the window of the bicycle shed, and after four years nobody expects to find out.

What we do know is that it happened (2)______ a Saturday afternoon in June, because Mr Hussain (3)______ (repair) his gate at the time and heard the glass go.

By the time he reached the shed, whoever (4)______ done it had gone. There was nothing there (5)______ a cricket ball, which he kept on his shelf for a fortnight in case somebody came to claim it.

Nobody did. (6)______ the third week, he gave it to the boy on the ninth floor, (7)______ had been watching the shelf with obvious longing.

The window (8)______ (replace) the following month. The town council sent a letter asking whether anyone had information, and every single resident wrote back to say that they had (9)______ .

I have often wondered (10)______ the boy on the ninth floor still has that ball.

Learning to Cook

My father decided last year that I (11)______ learn to cook one dish properly before I turned thirteen. He chose chicken rice, (12)______ is harder than it sounds.

The first attempt was a disaster. I (13)______ (forget) to skim the stock, and the rice came out greasy. My father said nothing at all, which was (14)______ than any comment he could have made.

We tried again the following Sunday, and (15)______ Sunday after that for eleven weeks. (16)______ the sixth attempt I was producing something edible; (17)______ the tenth, my mother asked for a second helping without being prompted.

What I learnt was not really about chicken rice. It was that my father (18)______ (be) willing to spend eleven Sunday mornings on something I had not asked to learn.

He has never once mentioned it (19)______ . But every time I cook it now, I skim the stock twice, (20)______ he taught me.

answers.tip: The subject of the clause is a person.
Past continuous — it was in progress.
Passive — the window did not replace itself.
Non-defining clause referring to the dish.
His silence was harder to bear.
He has not raised it since.

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Because the lift was broken.
questions.m: Because the lift was broken, we took the stairs
questions.tip: A fragment needs a main clause added.

questions.q: Fix this run-on: It was raining, we stayed indoors.
questions.m: It was raining, so we stayed indoors
questions.tip: Also accept a full stop or a semicolon.

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Running all the way to the bus stop.
questions.m: Running all the way to the bus stop, I still missed the bus

questions.q: Fix this run-on: She studied hard she passed easily.
questions.m: She studied hard, so she passed easily

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Although he had practised for months.
questions.m: Although he had practised for months, he forgot his lines

questions.q: Fix this run-on: The shop was closed, we went to the market instead.
questions.m: The shop was closed, so we went to the market instead

questions.q: Fix this dangling modifier: Walking to school, the rain began to fall.
questions.m: Walking to school, I felt the rain begin to fall

questions.q: Fix this dangling modifier: Covered in mud, my mother told me to shower.
questions.m: Covered in mud, I was told by my mother to shower
questions.tip: Also accept: My mother told me to shower because I was covered in mud.

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Which was the reason we left early.
questions.m: The lift was broken, which was the reason we left early

questions.q: Fix this run-on: He apologised, she forgave him.
questions.m: He apologised, and she forgave him

questions.q: Join into one complex sentence: The bell rang. We packed our bags. We left.
questions.m: When the bell rang, we packed our bags and left

questions.q: Join into one complex sentence: It was late. We decided to stay.
questions.m: Because it was late, we decided to stay

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Such a long queue at the counter.
questions.m: There was such a long queue at the counter that we gave up

questions.q: Fix this run-on: My brother plays the drums my sister plays the flute.
questions.m: My brother plays the drums and my sister plays the flute

questions.q: Fix this dangling modifier: Barking loudly, I could not sleep because of the dog.
questions.m: Because the dog was barking loudly, I could not sleep

questions.q: Fix this fragment: To finish the project before Friday.
questions.m: We worked late to finish the project before Friday

questions.q: Fix this run-on: The test was difficult nobody complained.
questions.m: The test was difficult, but nobody complained

questions.q: Join into one sentence: The girl won the prize. She is in my class.
questions.m: The girl who won the prize is in my class

questions.q: Fix this fragment: After we had eaten our lunch.
questions.m: After we had eaten our lunch, we went for a walk

questions.q: Fix this run-on: I checked my answers twice, I still made a mistake.
questions.m: Although I checked my answers twice, I still made a mistake

questions.q: Rewrite as one simple sentence: The boy was tired. The boy was hungry.
questions.m: The boy was tired and hungry

questions.q: Rewrite as a compound sentence: It was hot. We stayed inside.
questions.m: It was hot, so we stayed inside
questions.tip: Two main clauses joined by a FANBOYS word.

questions.q: Rewrite as a complex sentence: It was hot. We stayed inside.
questions.m: Because it was hot, we stayed inside
questions.tip: One main clause plus a dependent clause.

questions.q: Fix this dangling modifier: Having finished the exam, the hall emptied quickly.
questions.m: Having finished the exam, the pupils left and the hall emptied quickly
questions.tip: The hall did not sit the exam.

questions.q: Fix this run-on: She reached the station, the train had already gone.
questions.m: When she reached the station, the train had already gone

questions.q: Fix this fragment: Even though nobody had asked him to.
questions.m: He cleared the whole classroom, even though nobody had asked him to

questions.q: Fix this run-on: The paint was still wet I touched it anyway.
questions.m: The paint was still wet, but I touched it anyway

questions.q: Join into one sentence: The book was on the shelf. I had been looking for it.
questions.m: The book which I had been looking for was on the shelf

questions.q: Fix this dangling modifier: Left in the sun, the ice cream melted quickly. (correct or not?)
questions.m: This one is already correct — the ice cream was indeed left in the sun
questions.tip: Not every opening phrase is dangling. Check whether it really describes the subject.

questions.q: Fix this run-on: He is only eight, he reads adult novels.
questions.m: Although he is only eight, he reads adult novels
